title: The history of food preservation
h1: The history of food preservation: salt, sugar, drying, canning and cold, and what each cost
dek: From sun-drying and salting to Appert's bottles, the pressure retort and the icebox. A dated, sourced map of how people kept food, and why practice so often ran ahead of understanding.
description: A sourced overview of drying, salting, curing, canning and refrigeration, with dates, what each method cost, and why old methods are not a modern safety guide.
recheck: If any listed source changes, when primary or museum sources on canning's origins and the early ice trade are added, or when dedicated sourced pieces on pickling, fermentation and root cellars exist.

safety_review.scope: Taxonomy does not gate this item, but the page discusses canning, curing and botulism and carries a context-dependent verdict panel; it contains no recipe, quantity, time or temperature. Requested for human read-through of the verdict panel and of the statement that low-acid foods need pressure canning (CDC, FSIS).

source_use.hist-food-si-cold: Underground cold stores and icehouses; natural ice harvest and Tudor; iceboxes; why cold won out; DOMELRE and the 1927 GE Monitor top.
source_use.hist-food-nps-icebox: 1847 ice shipments; ice factories; 1927 GE refrigerator; 85 percent of households by 1944.
source_use.usscm-brenckle-2019: 1812 contract for salt and saltpetre; bread baked dry.
source_use.hist-food-marcy-prairie-traveler-text: Desiccated vegetables in the Crimean war and Utah; canned vegetables not as portable; sealed-tin butter.
source_use.hist-food-monticello-meat: Enslaved workers salting and smoking pork at Monticello.
source_use.hist-food-headsmashedin: Blackfoot preparation of dry meat and pemmican for winter.
source_use.rmg-life-at-sea: Poor diet at sea causing malnutrition and scurvy.

source_use.cdc-botulism-prevention: Pressure canning for low-acid foods; toxin cannot be seen, smelled or tasted; if in doubt, throw it out.
